preamble: Devoicing of the voiced bilabial stop [b] to tenuis [p] is a common unconditioned or initial-position change. It occurred across most Xiang and southern Bingzhou Jin varieties of Chinese, where Middle Chinese voiced initials became unaspirated voiceless stops; in Oghuric Turkic (Chuvash pin 'thousand' vs Turkish bin); in Hmongic, where the lost voicing survives as a low tone register; in Kott and Arin among the Yeniseian languages; and in Chamorro, where p is the regular reflex of Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *b.

examples.note: Voiced initials give unaspirated voiceless initials in all tones in most Xiang varieties; Chengbu keeps ba7.
Voiced obstruents of Middle Chinese become tenuis in all four tones.
Oghuric initial *b- > p-; Turkish bin keeps b-.
Voiced initials devoice in Hmong; the old voicing survives as a low tone register
Kott and Arin devoice *b; Ket and Yugh keep b (бей bēj)
Blust (2000) gives p as the regular Chamorro reflex of PMP *b, an unconditioned devoicing.
